# Conduit / RealWorld domain vocabulary

This document defines terms used in Requirements and architecture work for the [Conduit](https://github.com/gothinkster/realworld) (RealWorld) reference application. Canonical REST shapes live in `realworld/specs/api/openapi.yml`. UI routes, selectors, and browser storage are defined in [realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md](realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md). For an index of contracts, see [CONTRACTS.md](CONTRACTS.md). For system placement, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Product names

**RealWorld** is the cross-platform specification program (API, frontend E2E, documentation). **Conduit** is the blog-style demo product that implementations build: articles, authors, comments, and social features. The documentation site title is **RealWorld** per `realworld/docs/astro.config.mjs`.

## User and session

A **user** registers with email, username, and password. Login returns a JWT. The SPA stores the token under the **localStorage** key `jwtToken`. Protected API calls send `Authorization: Token <jwt>` (OpenAPI security scheme **Token**).

**Authentication** covers register, login, logout, and session persistence. E2E flows expect a signed-in user to see their profile in the navbar and to reach `/` after register or login. Failed auth surfaces `.error-messages` per the UI contract.

For test and debug hooks, conforming SPAs may expose `window.__conduit_debug__` with methods such as `getToken`, `getAuthState`, and `getCurrentUser` (contract in [realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md](realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md)).

## Article

An **article** has a title, description, body, optional **tag list**, author, and timestamps. The server assigns a **slug** from the title. The slug is the stable identifier in URLs and API paths (`/articles/{slug}`).

**Article lifecycle** (UI): create at `/editor`, publish, view at `/article/:slug`, edit at `/editor/:slug`, delete (typically returns to home). List rows use preview markup (for example `.article-preview`) per SELECTORS.md.

**Favorites**: a signed-in user can favorite or unfavorite an article. Favoriting updates counts and UI state. A user’s favorited articles appear on `/profile/:username/favorites`. API favorite operations are defined on article resources in `realworld/specs/api/openapi.yml`.

## Feed

**Global Feed** shows recent articles from all authors (home `/`, often the default tab). **Your Feed** shows articles from authors the current user **follows** only. E2E navigation and social specs switch between these feeds; both are first-class Conduit behaviors.

**Tag filter**: the sidebar lists **tags** (for example `.sidebar .tag-list .tag-pill`). Selecting a tag filters the article list, often via route `/tag/{tag}`.

**Pagination**: list endpoints and the UI use **offset** and **limit**. Conformance E2E may assert up to ten `.article-preview` rows on the first page when many articles are seeded.

## Profile and follow

A **profile** is a public author page at `/profile/:username`. It shows username, bio, image, and the user’s articles. **Settings** at `/settings` let the signed-in user update email, username, password, bio, and image (`PUT /user` in the API contract). After a successful settings save, flows often redirect to `/profile/{username}`.

**Follow** / **unfollow**: one user can follow another’s profile (`POST` and `DELETE` on `/profiles/{username}/follow` in OpenAPI). Following affects **Your Feed** content and profile button state. E2E helpers `followUser` and `unfollowUser` exercise this in the browser.

Demo or seeded users such as **johndoe** appear in cross-user scenarios when **EXTERNAL_API** test mode uses a live backend (inferred).

## Comment

A **comment** belongs to one article. On `/article/:slug`, the user writes in a field with placeholder text **Write a comment...** and posts via **Post Comment**; comments render as cards. The article or comment author may **delete** a comment via mod-options UI, per comments E2E and SELECTORS.md.

## API vocabulary (REST)

Base URL in the reference spec is `https://api.realworld.show/api` (overridable in tests via `API_BASE` in `realworld/specs/e2e/helpers/config.ts`). Common path groups:

| Area | Paths (representative) |
|------|-------------------------|
| Auth | `/users`, `/users/login`, `/user` |
| Profiles | `/profiles/{username}`, `/profiles/{username}/follow` |
| Articles | `/articles`, `/articles/feed`, `/articles/{slug}`, favorites on article resources |
| Comments | `/articles/{slug}/comments` |
| Tags | `/tags` |

Request bodies often wrap entities (`user`, `article`, `comment`) as in OpenAPI. Full operation list: `realworld/specs/api/openapi.yml`.

## UI routes (SPA)

Routes exercised by the shared Playwright suite include:

| Route | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `/` | Home, Global Feed (and tag-filtered list) |
| `/login`, `/register` | Authentication |
| `/editor`, `/editor/:slug` | Create, edit article |
| `/article/:slug` | Read article, comments |
| `/settings` | Account settings |
| `/profile/:username` | Author profile and articles |
| `/profile/:username/favorites` | Favorited articles |
| `/tag/:tag` | Articles filtered by tag |

Angular implementation routing lives under `src/app`; see [src/app/AGENTS.md](src/app/AGENTS.md).

## Test mode terms (E2E)

These flags gate shared E2E behavior; they are not end-user product terms but matter for interpreting specs:

- **TEST_MODE** — implementation architecture class for the suite (`spa`, `ssr`, `fullstack` per helpers).
- **BROWSER_API** — SPA-only tests: `page.route` mocks, `localStorage` token cases, optional `window.__conduit_debug__`, and HTTP status nuances (for example article delete 200 vs 204).
- **EXTERNAL_API** — tests that register users or seed articles via the live API (`registerUserViaAPI`, `createManyArticles`, and related helpers) instead of UI-only setup.

Details: [GUIDELINES.md](GUIDELINES.md) and `realworld/specs/e2e/helpers/config.ts`.

## Null and display conventions

**Null fields**: when the API returns null or empty for **image**, **bio**, or settings fields, the UI must not show the literal string `null`. Conforming frontends use **default-avatar.svg** for missing images and empty strings in forms and profile copy (null-fields E2E).

## Error handling (UI)

When API calls fail, conforming SPAs show errors in **`.error-messages`** and keep core chrome (for example `nav.navbar`) usable. Error-handling E2E may mock `https://api.realworld.show/api` to assert 400, 401, 403, 404, malformed JSON, and empty bodies.
